title: PySpark: clean, cast and join raw orders
objective_text: Turn raw text orders into a typed Silver table with PySpark: tidy and filter on status, cast each column, drop incomplete and duplicate rows, and add each product's category with a left join.
scenario: Orders land in the Bronze lakehouse as text, straight from a CSV export: statuses in any case with stray spaces, some rows without a date or a quantity, and a few orders sent twice. Sales wants a Silver orders table with real types, one row per completed order and each product's category, including orders for products that aren't in the product list yet.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: Delta tables bronze.raw_orders and bronze.products in the exercise folder, and a starter answer.py.
required: Only completed orders, whatever the case of status or the spaces around it.
order_id and qty are integers, order_date is a date and amount is a decimal.
No row without an order_date or a qty, and one row per order_id.
category comes from bronze.products; an order whose product isn't there keeps its row with category 'unknown'.
Write silver.orders with order_id, order_date, product_id, category, qty, amount, so that running the code again leaves the same table.

expected.description: silver.orders has 5 rows: orders 1, 2, 5, 7 and 8, once each; order 5's category is unknown.

verifies: Your PySpark cleans, casts, deduplicates and left-joins the exercise data and rows you haven't seen, on this PC.
silver.orders has the columns asked for, one row per order_id and no missing key values.
Running it again leaves the same table.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in a Fabric notebook, so it doesn't show how Spark plans the join, how it behaves on large tables, or Spark's own casting rules for text it can't parse.
That the table is a lakehouse table in OneLake: here it's a Delta table in the exercise folder on this PC.
The SQL and KQL parts of the objective, which other exercises cover.

validation.pass: silver.orders holds the right rows for the practice data.
validation.fail: silver.orders doesn't match: check the status filter, the missing values and the join.

validation.pass: It also works on data you haven't seen.
validation.fail: It doesn't hold on other data: avoid relying on these exact rows.

validation.pass: The columns, types and keys are right.
validation.fail: A column, a type or a key is off: see the detail.

validation.pass: Running it twice leaves the same table.
validation.fail: A second run changed the table: write with overwrite.

hints: F.lower(F.trim(F.col("status"))) turns ' Complete ' into 'complete'; filter on that.
F.col("qty").cast("int") and .cast("date") give real types; a missing value stays null, so filter with isNotNull() after casting.
dropDuplicates(["order_id"]) keeps one row per order.
how="left" keeps order 5, whose product isn't listed; F.coalesce(F.col("category"), F.lit("unknown")) labels it.
Write with mode("overwrite") so a rerun replaces the table.
explanation: Clean before you cast and filter: trim and lower status so every spelling of 'complete' matches, cast each text column to its type, then drop rows that still lack a date or a quantity. Remove the duplicate order before the join so it can't multiply, left-join products so an order for an unlisted product stays, and label its category instead of leaving it null. Compute amount from the typed columns and overwrite the table, so a rerun gives the same Silver table.
troubleshooting: Order 2 or 8 is missing: status still has spaces or capitals; trim and lower it before filtering.
Order 5 is missing: the join is inner; use a left join.
Order 7 appears twice: drop duplicates on order_id.
The table doubles on a second run: write with mode("overwrite").
reset: Reset rebuilds the bronze tables from setup.sql, removes silver.orders and puts the starter back.
review_notes: The raw data has missing values but no unparseable text, because DuckDB's CAST raises an error where Spark (with ANSI mode off) returns null. The does_not_verify line says Spark's casting rules aren't shown.
